```{r data generation, echo = FALSE, results = "hide"}
dat <- matrix(c(
  "STUDENT_ID", "Primary Key of STUDENT table",
  "COURSE_ID", "Primary Key of COURSE table",
  "PROFESSOR_ID", "Primary Key of PROFESSOR table",
  "ENROLLMENT_ID", "Primary Key of ENROLLMENT table",
  "STUDENT.NAME", "Attribute of STUDENT entity",
  "COURSE.TITLE", "Attribute of COURSE entity",
  "PROFESSOR.EMAIL", "Attribute of PROFESSOR entity",
  "ENROLLMENT.STUDENT_ID", "Foreign Key referencing STUDENT",
  "ENROLLMENT.COURSE_ID", "Foreign Key referencing COURSE",
  "COURSE.PROFESSOR_ID", "Foreign Key referencing PROFESSOR",
  "STUDENT", "Entity representing university students",
  "COURSE", "Entity representing university courses",
  "PROFESSOR", "Entity representing instructors",
  "ENROLLMENT", "Associative entity connecting students and courses"), 
  nrow = 2)
i <- sample(1:ncol(dat), 1)
iso <- dat[1, i]
ctr <- dat[2, i]
```

Question
========
There are several tables in the university's database: STUDENT, COURSE, PROFESSOR and ENROLMENT. In this relational database, what `r ctr` stands for?

Solution
========
`r ctr` is `r iso`.
